title: Hari Krishnan – Hedging a Commodity Bull Market (S7E4)

reader_summary.headline: All right, three, two, one, let's jam.
reader_summary.overview: All right, three, two, one, let's jam. All opinions expressed by podcasts. participants are solely their own opinion and do not reflect the opinion of newfound research. In this episode, I am joined by Hari Krishnan, head of volatility strategies at SCT Capital.

key_points.text: In this episode, I am joined by Hari Krishnan, head of volatility strategies at SCT Capital.
key_points.evidence_quote: In this episode, I am joined by Hari Krishnan, head of volatility strategies at SCT Capital, and author of the book's second leg down and market tremors.

key_points.text: This is Hari's second appearance on the show, but he comes to us with a very different topic.
key_points.evidence_quote: This is Hari's second appearance on the show, but he comes to us with a very different topic, how to develop a low-carry hedge for a commodity bull market.

key_points.text: Taking a similar line of thinking to his book market tremors.
key_points.evidence_quote: Taking a similar line of thinking to his book market tremors, Hari evaluates the market market through the perspective of both commodity producers and consumers.
By understanding their business incentives, Hari believes he's better able to understand their market positioning and the potential imbalances created in both futures and options markets.

thesis: The episode discusses a client's request to approximate physical commodity ownership using financial instruments to capture upside in a bull market without incurring high roll costs associated with contango. The speaker proposes a solution involving two sides: a discretionary approach to identify cheap commodities with catalysts and an engineering approach to capture upside with minimal carry costs.
